record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: automatic finite potential energy for entire Ginzburg-Landau solutions
record.original_question: For a smooth map u: R^2 -> R^2 satisfying the entire Ginzburg-Landau equation Delta u = u(1 - |u|^2) and the condition |u(x)| -> 1 as |x| -> infinity, must the finite-potential-energy condition integral_{R^2} (|u|^2 - 1)^2 < infinity automatically hold?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.5 ([25, Problem 2], [13, Open Problem 2]). Assume that u satisfies (2.4) and (2.5). Does (2.7) hold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $u\colon \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth map satisfying the Ginzburg–Landau equation
\[
\Delta u = u\bigl(|u|^2 - 1\bigr) \quad \text{on } \mathbb{R}^2,
\]
together with the boundary condition at infinity
\[
|u(x)| \to 1 \quad \text{as } |x| \to \infty.
\]
Must $u$ then automatically satisfy the finite potential energy condition
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \bigl(|u|^2 - 1\bigr)^2 \, dx < \infty\, ?
\]
Equivalently, does pointwise convergence of $|u|$ to $1$ at infinity for an entire solution of the planar Ginzburg–Landau equation force quadratic integrability of $|u|^2 - 1$?
artifact.status_search_result: No source located in the search establishes a resolution of this specific implication ("|u|→1 at infinity implies ∫(|u|²−1)² < ∞" for entire planar Ginzburg–Landau solutions). It is listed as an open problem in Brezis-type problem collections and is referenced through standard problem lists (Bethuel–Brezis–Hélein Problem 2; Brezis "Open Problem 2"). A recent 2025 preprint by Wei et al. announces a complete solution to "Brezis' First Open Problem," which concerns the classification/uniqueness of degree ±1 entire solutions rather than this automatic-finite-energy question. Hence this problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Some of my favorite open problems — Haïm Brezis
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems on entire Ginzburg–Landau solutions, including the question whether |u|→1 at infinity yields finite potential energy.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is recorded as an open problem in Brezis's collection.

status_evidence.title: On Brezis' First Open Problem: A Complete Solution
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves Brezis's first open problem regarding classification of entire Ginzburg–Landau solutions of degree ±1, not the finite potential energy implication considered here.
status_evidence.claim: A different Brezis open problem on Ginzburg–Landau was resolved in 2025; the present problem is not addressed there.

status_evidence.title: New developments on the Ginzburg–Landau model — H. Brezis
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses entire Ginzburg–Landau solutions and lists associated open questions about asymptotic behavior and finite potential energy.
status_evidence.claim: The automatic-finite-energy question is repeatedly cited as open in Brezis's surveys.
